key: Verily in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest!
s: Answering the call for a sign, the surah describes those God guides; Ibn Kathir, on 13:27 to 13:29, takes such rest as hearts leaning towards God, content with Him as protector and helper, and this line as saying He is worthy of it.
src: Ibn Kathir, Tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-ʿAẓīm, on 13:27 to 13:29, Tarteel QUL Arabic text via spa5k/tafsir_api, commit 9ae590a (2026)

evidence.words: ﴿الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَتَطْمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُمْ بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ﴾ أَيْ: تَطِيبُ وَتَرْكَنُ إِلَى جَانِبِ اللَّهِ، وَتَسْكُنُ عِنْدَ ذِكْرِهِ، وَتَرْضَى بِهِ مَوْلًى وَنَصِيرًا؛ وَلِهَذَا قَالَ: ﴿أَلا بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ الْقُلُوبُ﴾ أَيْ: هُوَ حَقِيقٌ بِذَلِكَ
evidence.gloss: (Those who believe and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of God:) that is, they grow glad and lean towards God’s side, settle at His remembrance, and are content with Him as protector and helper; and for this He said (Verily in the remembrance of God do hearts find rest), that is, He is worthy of that.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Ar-Ra’d 13:28, at 1734), the second sentence of the ayah. Plain sense faithful: 13:27 has the disbelievers ask for a portent and the answer that God guides those who turn to Him, described in 13:28; no four-word run from the verse. Ibn Kathir’s one comment on 13:27 to 13:29 glosses the rest as hearts growing glad, leaning to God’s side, settling at His remembrance and content with Him as protector and helper, and glosses the closing line as He is worthy of that. The sentence says no more than that. Evidence cut by script from the packet. Entry-check ok.
